title: Latent Variable Modeling with Logit-Beta Models
text: logit-beta latent variable modeling (lblvm) framework can viewed alongside two well-established latent variable modeling traditions: factor analysis (FA) item response theory (IRT). Conventional FA models typically formulated identity link normally distribution, whereas IRT generally uses logit link (probit link) Bernoulli categorical distribution. underlying premise logit-beta framework parallel FA IRT: observed responses can interpreted manifestations one unobserved continuous latent variables. framework conceptually similar FA modeling responses continuous probability distribution, sharing IRT property mean-dependent conditional variance. Unlike homoscedastic normal distribution typically used FA, variance beta distribution depends mean. result, intercept plays prominent role, similar role IRT. framework accommodates bounded-continuous ordered categorical responses. Bounded-continuous responses can naturally modeled using beta distribution (Li & Shin, 2025). ordered categorical responses, discretized response model (DRM) assumes observed categories arise discretization underlying bounded-continuous response process, category probabilities determined intervals bounded continuum (Li & Jeon, review).

title: Bayes Factor from Laplace Approximation — BF
text: Let \(D\) denote observed data, \(\tau\) parameter vector, \(M_k\) model hypothesis indexed \(k\). marginal probability data \(M_k\) $$   I_k = P(D \mid M_k)       = \int P(D \mid \tau, M_k)\pi(\tau \mid M_k)\,d\tau, $$ \(\pi(\tau \mid M_k)\) prior density \(\tau\). marginal probability approximated using Laplace approximation: $$   I_k \approx   (2\pi)^{d/2}   \lvert\hat{\Sigma}\rvert^{1/2}   P(D \mid \hat{\tau}, M_k)   \pi(\hat{\tau} \mid M_k), $$ \(d\) dimension parameter vector, \(\hat{\tau}\) mode posterior distribution, \(\hat{\Sigma}^{-1}\) Fisher information matrix. example, log_marginal_M0 denotes \(\log I_0\), log marginal probability data Model 0.

text: formula character string specifying predetermined model structure. See examples supported specification. data matrix data frame item responses. t_prior numeric vector specifying standard deviations threshold priors. range numeric vector specifying range latent trait values grid approximation dimension. Defaults c(-4, 4). q integer specifying number grid points per latent trait dimension grid approximation. Defaults 41. ngrid integer specifying number grid points 0--1 range grid approximation. Defaults 1000. max_iter integer specifying maximum number iterations optimization. Defaults 200 EM 400 MHRM. threshold numeric value specifying convergence threshold. Defaults 0.000001 EM, based gradient convergence criterion, 0.001 MHRM, based maximum parameter change. EM, gradient convergence criterion defined \(\frac{\mathbf{g}'(\mathbf{H} + \mathbf{J})^{-1}\mathbf{g}}   {|\log \mathcal{L}| + \delta}\). eq_interval logical value indicating whether category intervals equally spaced. Defaults FALSE. estimation character string specifying estimation method: EM expectation-maximization algorithm MHRM Metropolis-Hastings Robbins-Monro algorithm. est_cov logical value indicating whether estimate covariance matrix latent variables \(\theta\).
